We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a \u0026quot;normalized\u0026quot; problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/div\u0026gt;\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Available Locations\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Austin, US\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;San Francisco, CA\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;About the Role\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Cloudflare built its reputation helping build a better Internet, defending millions of sites, giving away SSL and DDoS mitigation when the industry charged premium prices. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Rapid response.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare\u0026#39;s infrastructure and the customer\u0026#39;s stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Proactive engineering.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Responsibilities\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;Rapid response:\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own a Sev-1 incident where a large financial services customer sees asymmetric latency from a single POP. Trace it through BGP routing and origin configuration. Produce the fix upstream.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Diagnose a recurring WebSocket disconnect that a media customer has been fighting for weeks. Isolate it to a specific interaction between WAF and their origin load balancer. Drive the fix with Product Engineering.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Partner with a government customer\u0026#39;s SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;Proactive engineering:\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Build, with Product Engineering, a distributed tracing capability that correlates Cloudflare edge signals with customer origin metrics so a single query tells the story of a failing request end-to-end.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Ship a detector for a class of WAF false positives silently degrading several customers. Get it into production before the next renewal cycle.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Prototype an AI agent that takes a new customer case, pulls relevant logs and config, and proposes a root cause with linked evidence. Deploy it internally. Measure whether it makes engineers faster. Iterate.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Rapid incident response and root cause analysis.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Own the most complex, high-severity customer issues end-to-end, from first signal through confirmed resolution. Lead deep-dive debugging across the full stack: edge, network, DNS, transport, APIs, application, customer-side configuration. Reproduce defects, validate fixes with Engineering, and confirm customer-side resolution. Produce postmortems other engineers rely on. Hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global rotation that includes weekends.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Proactive reliability engineering.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Analyze support and telemetry signals across the customer base to find systemic risks before they become incidents. Contribute monitoring, detection, and diagnostic capability to the core product and the engineering systems that give Customer Support early visibility into customer-affecting issues. Define customer-facing reliability metrics (error rates, resolution times, repeat-contact rates) and drive measurable improvement. Write automation that reduces mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Cross-functional partnership.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Manage the technical escalation lifecycle with clear ownership and timely communication. Partner with Product Engineering to drive fixes, workarounds, and configuration changes that address underlying gaps. Represent the customer reliability perspective in engineering syncs, incident reviews, and post-mortem processes.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Technical leadership and enablement.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Raise the technical floor of Customer Support through pair-debugging, structured knowledge transfer, and shared tooling. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a \u0026quot;normalized\u0026quot; problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/div\u0026gt;\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Available Locations: Lisbon, Portugal or London, UK\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About the Role\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Cloudflare built its reputation helping build a better Internet, defending millions of sites, giving away SSL and DDoS mitigation when the industry charged premium prices. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;The Role\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Rapid response.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare\u0026#39;s infrastructure and the customer\u0026#39;s stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Proactive engineering.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;What You Might Work On\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Rapid response:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;Own a Sev-1 incident where a large financial services customer sees asymmetric latency from a single POP. Trace it through BGP routing and identify transit provider policy change that is required to resolve.\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;Diagnose a recurring WebSocket disconnect a media customer has been experiencing across multiple release cycles. Isolate it to a specific interaction between a Cloudflare service release and the customer\u0026#39;s connection lifecycle. Drive the fix with the owning engineering team.\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;Partner with a government customer\u0026#39;s SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Proactive engineering:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Build, with Product Engineering, a distributed tracing capability that correlates Cloudflare edge signals with customer origin metrics so a single query tells the story of a failing request end-to-end.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Ship a detector for a class of WAF false positives silently degrading several customers. Get it into production before the next renewal cycle.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Prototype an AI agent that takes a new customer case, pulls relevant logs and config, and proposes a root cause with linked evidence. Deploy it internally. Measure whether it makes engineers faster. Iterate.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Responsibilities\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Rapid incident response and root cause analysis.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Own the most complex, high-severity customer issues end-to-end, from first signal through confirmed resolution. Lead deep-dive debugging across the full stack: edge, network, DNS, transport, APIs, application, customer-side configuration. Reproduce defects, validate fixes with Engineering, and confirm customer-side resolution. Produce postmortems other engineers rely on. Hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global rotation that includes weekends.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Proactive reliability engineering.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Analyze support and telemetry signals across the customer base to find systemic risks before they become incidents. Contribute monitoring, detection, and diagnostic capability to the core product and the engineering systems that give Customer Support early visibility into customer-affecting issues. Define customer-facing reliability metrics (error rates, resolution times, repeat-contact rates) and drive measurable improvement. Write automation that reduces mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Cross-functional partnership.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Manage the technical escalation lifecycle with clear ownership and timely communication. People increasingly get answers from AI instead of a list of links, agents run dozens of searches to answer a single question, and \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://blog.cloudflare.com/agentic-web/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;more than half of the traffic reaching sites on Cloudflare is now automated\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;. Search is shifting from a destination to a utility, and Cloudflare is building the search layer for this agentic Internet.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Agentic Search at Cloudflare gives agents everything they need to find information, whether it lives in a customer’s own data or on the open web. It spans two products: AI Search for internal data, and Web Search API for the open web.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;AI Search\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt; (internal data), \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://blog.cloudflare.com/ai-search-ga/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;now generally available\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, is the \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://blog.cloudflare.com/ai-search-agent-primitive/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;search primitive for applications and agents\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;. It is a fully managed indexing and retrieval pipeline built on \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;Workers AI\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/vectorize/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;Vectorize\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;R2\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, and \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;Browser Run\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;. Developers connect a website or R2 bucket, or upload their own files, and query them with natural language through a Workers binding, REST API, or MCP server. Under the hood: continuous indexing, hybrid vector and keyword retrieval, reranking, metadata filtering, native multimodal (image) embeddings, and OCR for scanned documents. We use it to power search on our own blog and developer docs.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-search/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;Web Search API\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt; (external data), \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-introducing-web-search-api/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;now in open beta\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, gives agents real-time web context with a single API call. It runs on \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;AI Gateway\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, so every search gets the same logging, analytics, billing, and access controls as model inference. Developers can choose from \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-search/providers/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;multiple search providers\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt; and always get results back in one normalized format.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Your mission in this role is to make Cloudflare the default place developers and agents go to search, across both their own data and the open web, and eventually in a single call. You’ll also help build a search ecosystem that works for AI companies, site owners, and creators alike.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;What You’ll Site owners have it worse: AI crawlers already request content anywhere from a hundred to tens of thousands of times for every visitor they send back, and most have no idea how, or whether, they show up in AI answers. Both sides of the market are flying blind.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Cloudflare sits in front of around 20% of the web and sees both sides of that exchange. Signals \u0026amp;amp; Data Products turns our network\u0026#39;s view into products both sides can use: helping AI labs know what\u0026#39;s fresh and trustworthy, and helping site owners see and shape how they show up in AI. You\u0026#39;ll work with engineering, construction, procurement, and operations teams to ensure facilities, equipment, and site services are ready when they\u0026#39;re needed, with clear accountability for schedule, cost, and quality.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;What you\u0026#39;ll do:\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Deliver data centers\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Represent Cloudflare across new builds and expansions, managing data center providers, general contractors, design consultants, commissioning agents, and compute integration partners.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Coordinate mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) installation, white space fit-out, rack-level power, structured cabling, equipment staging and validation, and commissioning through operational acceptance.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Maintain a delivery schedule that connects construction milestones, equipment arrivals, service activation, and deployment dependencies. Resolve field issues and drive recovery plans when commitments slip.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Assess vendor and partner readiness before deployment, and coordinate handover with operations so acceptance criteria, documentation, and support responsibilities are clear.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Source site services and manage contracts\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own sourcing for the services each site needs to open and operate, including temporary power and water, security, waste management, and facilities support.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Translate construction and operational requirements into scopes of work, supplier selections, and service start dates. Identify gaps early enough to prevent delays to site work.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Negotiate regional and multi-site agreements, rate cards, service-level commitments, and change orders that new sites can use without restarting procurement.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Hold suppliers accountable for delivery, service quality, and commercial commitments, coordinating utility and service-provider dependencies with construction and operations.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Manage the portfolio\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Track budgets, forecasts, scope changes, and risks across concurrent projects. Apply lessons from each build to the next.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Ensure deployment activities meet applicable codes, safety standards, and security requirements in partnership with the responsible technical teams.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;What you\u0026#39;ll bring:\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;7+ years Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/div\u0026gt;\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Available Location: Singapore\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About the Department\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Cloudforce One\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; is Cloudflare\u0026#39;s threat operations and research team, responsible for identifying and disrupting cyber threats ranging from sophisticated cyber criminal activity to nation-state sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs). Cloudforce One works in close partnership with external organizations and internal Cloudflare teams, continuously developing operational tradecraft and expanding ever-growing sources of threat intelligence to enable expedited threat hunting and remediation.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Members of Cloudforce One are at the helm of leveraging an incredibly vast and varied set of data points that only one of the world\u0026#39;s largest global networks can provide. The team analyzes these unique data points at massive scale and efficiency, synthesizing findings into actionable threat intelligence to better protect our customers.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About INTERDICT\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;I.N.T.E.R.D.I.C.T.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; (Identify, Neutralize, Triage, Engage, Respond, Disrupt, Integrate, Contain, Threat Hunting) is Cloudforce One\u0026#39;s unified operational security organization responsible for identifying, analyzing, and responding to threats targeting Cloudflare and its customers. INTERDICT encompasses three main sub-functions:\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Cloudflare Managed Defense (CMD):\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Network and application security monitoring for \u0026#39;Under Attack\u0026#39; mitigation support.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;PhishGuard:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Managed email threat detection and response service.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Detection Engineering:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; ML model development and detection optimization.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Together, INTERDICT provides comprehensive \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;24×7×365 protection\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; across email, application, and network threat surfaces.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Role Summary\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;As a \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Senior Response Engineer\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; within the Cloudflare Managed Defense Center (CMDC), you will serve as a subject-matter expert and technical escalation point for threat mitigation across Cloudflare’s strategic enterprise customer base. In this role, you will lead the response to sophisticated, multi-vector cyberattacks spanning OSI Layers 3, 4, and 7, operating beyond standard playbooks to diagnose anomalies, engineer custom mitigations, and stabilize mission-critical infrastructure under fire.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Beyond active incident command, you will act as a force multiplier: architecting customer-specific defense strategies, authoring and refining automated detection logic, mentoring Tier 1 and Tier 2 engineers, and collaborating directly with Cloudflare Product and Engineering teams. We are looking for an experienced, high-ownership technical leader who excels during high-stakes incidents and is passionate about mentoring others while advancing threat mitigation at scale.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;CMDC operates 24×7×365. \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;This role participates in a regional shift rotation and on-call escalation rota including periodic weekend and public-holiday coverage as part of a follow-the-sun model across AMER, EMEA, and APAC.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Role Responsibilities\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Act as the technical lead and incident commander during high-impact, multi-vector security events, designing and deploying bespoke mitigation strategies when standard runbooks do not suffice.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Perform deep-dive forensic analysis into complex Layer 3/4 and Layer 7 traffic anomalies, identifying zero-day attack patterns, sophisticated bot networks, and novel evasion techniques.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Apply advanced mitigation strategies and filter malicious traffic using Cloudflare’s core security suite, including Magic Transit, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Advanced Rate Limiting.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Lead technical communications and incident bridge calls with enterprise C-level executives, principal network engineers, and security teams during critical events, clearly articulating root causes, impact assessments, and remediation paths.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Monitor and investigate proactive security alerts across internal telemetry systems to rapidly triage incoming events, assess blast radius, and validate threat severity.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Adhere to and champion strict customer SLAs for alert response times, event analysis, and clear executive reporting.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Mentor and elevate Tier 1 and Tier 2 engineers through structured shadowing, technical post-mortems, and internal training.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Partner with internal Engineering and Product teams to translate operational attack trends into prioritized platform enhancements, tool feedback, and automated detection logic.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Role Requirements (Must-Have Skills)\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A minimum of 6–8 years of hands-on experience in a high-volume Security Operations Center (SOC), Managed Detection and Response (MDR), network engineering, or incident response environment dealing directly with live threat mitigation.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Comprehensive analyzing network traffic data for anomaly detection and designing, tuning, and executing advanced mitigation strategies against L3/L4 and L7 attacks, including bespoke countermeasures when standard playbooks are insufficient.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Advanced proficiency in packet capture and network traffic analysis using tools such as tcpdump, Wireshark, or tshark to isolate paired with the hands-on capability to build and integrate custom tooling that improves operational workflows, accelerates log telemetry analysis, and defends against AI-driven botnets and adversarial edge attacks.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Proficiency in using the command line (Bash shell) alongside general system administration literacy across Linux, Mac, or Windows environments.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Proven experience commanding incident bridges, making decisive risk-tradeoff decisions, and maintaining composure while managing enterprise stakeholders during high-pressure crises.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Nice-to-Have Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;About the Team\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We build the infrastructure that makes the web \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Payable\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;, powering the future of machine-to-machine commerce.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Here at Cloudflare, agentic commerce is a core part of our vision for the \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://blog.cloudflare.com/the-agentic-internet/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;Agentic Internet\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;. As AI agents increasingly navigate, consume, and act on the web, standard payment and authorization models built for humans are breaking down. We build tools that make the new internet payable by giving our users the ability to monetize access to their content, data, services, products, and outcomes across the Internet, regardless of where they are hosted.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Building these capabilities requires solving complex engineering problems across high-throughput web infrastructure, low-latency transaction processing, usage metering, outcome verification, digital wallets, and emerging agentic payment protocols (such as x402, WBA, ACP, and UCP). Hyperdrive is a core piece of the Cloudflare Developer Platform that accelerates database queries from Cloudflare Workers by pooling connections and caching data at the edge. By eliminating the massive latency overhead of TCP, TLS, and database-specific handshakes, Hyperdrive allows developers to use the databases they already know and love—like PostgreSQL and MySQL—without the \u0026quot;cold start\u0026quot; performance penalties typically associated with serverless environments.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;Responsibilities\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Hyperdrive is integrated directly into the Cloudflare global network and features:\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Global Connection Pooling: Maintains \u0026quot;warm\u0026quot; connections to origin databases across the globe, reducing connection times by up to 90%.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Intelligent Query Caching: Automatically caches frequently run read queries as close to the user as possible.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Protocol-Aware Proxying: Features custom-built implementations of database wire protocols (PostgreSQL and MySQL) to parse and optimize traffic in real-time.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Seamless Integration: Works with existing ORMs and drivers, providing a simple connection string that \u0026quot;just works\u0026quot; for developers.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;The team is geographically distributed across North America.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;You will own your code from inception to release, delivering solutions at all layers of the software stack to empower Cloudflare customers. On any given day, you might write a design document that outlines how you plan to solve a specific problem, or fix a bug in how our user experience renders. Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p class=\u0026quot;doc-paragraph\u0026quot;\u0026gt;The \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Cloudflare Queues\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;\u0026amp;nbsp;team builds a managed, global message queuing service for developers. Queues allows customers to send, buffer, and reliably deliver messages between Workers with at-least-once delivery, batching, and configurable delivery guarantees, without managing infrastructure or paying bandwidth egress fees. Deeply integrated with Cloudflare Workers, Queues supports event-driven and asynchronous applications across the Developer Platform. Generally available since September 2024, Queues runs at global scale on Cloudflare’s edge network and is a foundational building block for event-driven and asynchronous applications.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p class=\u0026quot;doc-paragraph\u0026quot;\u0026gt;In this role, you will help design and build \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Cloudflare Queues\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, improving reliability, performance, and delivery guarantees while shipping new features at global scale. The R2 Gateway team owns the request-facing layer of R2 — the S3-compatible API gateway that every object put, get, list, and delete flows through. When a customer or application talks to R2, they talk to the systems we build and operate.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;R2 is growing rapidly, and the gateway must evolve to keep pace. The team is responsible for the API surface that handles authentication, request routing, rate limiting, and coordination between clients and R2\u0026#39;s storage and metadata layers — all while maintaining strict compatibility with the S3 API and delivering low-latency, highly available access at global scale.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You\u0026#39;ll be joining a team that operates at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, storage infrastructure, and edge computing — building request-path systems that need to be correct, fast, and reliable on every single call.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;Responsibilities\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Design, implement, and operate the S3-compatible API gateway that serves every R2 operation, ensuring correctness, low latency, and compatibility with the S3 API surface.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Build and operate production services on Cloudflare Workers and Kubernetes that handle high-throughput request traffic with strong availability and durability guarantees.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own the request path end to end — authentication, authorization, routing, rate limiting, and error handling — and the interfaces between the gateway and R2\u0026#39;s storage and metadata layers.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own projects end to end: from design docs through implementation, testing, deployment, and production monitoring.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Continuously improve the reliability, performance, and observability of the gateway; ramp quickly into unfamiliar and legacy code paths and reduce operational toil.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Participate in on-call rotations, drive incident resolution, and write postmortems that raise reliability standards.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Use AI tools extensively to accelerate development, debugging, and operational tasks. Build secure, reliable networking capabilities using technologies such as IPsec, MASQUE, eBPF, and Linux kernel networking primitives while keeping the system small, predictable, and secure.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Engineer reliable fleet control:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Build distributed control-plane and state-management systems that safely deliver configuration and commands, tolerate intermittent connectivity and partial failures, converge to known-good state, and support zero-touch operation across large device fleets.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Secure the device lifecycle:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Improve hardware-backed identity, attestation, secure boot, immutable operating-system images, credential rotation, and staged over-the-air upgrades with safe rollback and recovery.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Make operability a product feature:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Design telemetry, diagnostics, synthetic tests, support bundles, and remote operations that help customers and support teams understand the system without treating the appliance as a black box.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Drive customer-centered product decisions:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; Work with customers, Product, Support, and Solutions Engineering to understand customer requirements and turn them into pragmatic technical direction. Our Network Services product suite (Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, Spectrum, and more) puts the connectivity, scale, and performance of Cloudflare\u0026#39;s global network in front of customers\u0026#39; applications, network infrastructure, and private networks, providing a single pane of glass for network connectivity, visibility, and network functions like DDoS protection, firewalling, and load balancing. We are a team of engineers and product managers who obsess over quickly building products that solve real customer problems, using techniques that take advantage of Cloudflare\u0026#39;s unique architecture and global network footprint.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Our teams build and operate the software behind these products: the data plane that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare\u0026#39;s network, the on-ramps and routing that get traffic to and from customers, and the control planes and APIs that configure all of it. We own what we build in production, and a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;About the role\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We\u0026#39;re hiring engineers at several levels across a few closely related teams. There\u0026#39;s one application and one interview process, and we\u0026#39;ll work out with you which team fits your interests and experience. Some of the things these teams work on:\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;The data plane behind Magic Transit and Cloudflare WAN, including Unified Routing (our userspace forwarding plane, which gives each customer flexible forwarding of their traffic) and Fast-Path, which uses XDP and eBPF to forward very large single flows\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;The on-ramps customers use to reach us (GRE, IPsec, PNI), and the tunnel health checks that move traffic away from failing paths\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;An anycast BGP implementation for customer tunnels, where sessions survive being moved between servers and data centers\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Cloudflare Network Firewall, a low-latency userspace packet firewall written in Rust, with rate limiting, intrusion detection, and packet capture\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Unimog, our XDP-based L4 load balancer, which touches nearly every connection into Cloudflare and forwards packets between servers and between data centers\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Spectrum, a TCP/UDP reverse proxy written in Go that brings Cloudflare\u0026#39;s network to non-HTTP applications (e.g., gaming, SSH, MQTT, custom protocols, ...), plus TCP Workers\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;The APIs and control plane systems that let customers express complex network configurations simply, and that push that configuration to every server in our network\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You\u0026#39;ll build, deploy, and operate your team\u0026#39;s systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. Most of our code is Go and Rust (plus C for eBPF) on Linux, and the work ranges from kernel networking (XDP, tc, netfilter, namespaces) through userspace packet processing to distributed systems and APIs. You\u0026#39;ll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our teams and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We\u0026#39;re looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done!\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Examples of desirable skills, knowledge, and experience\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Systems programming experience, especially in Go, Rust, or C\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A solid understanding of L3 and L4 networking: IP, TCP, UDP, routing, tunneling (GRE, IPsec), NAT, and anycast; More than 50% of Internet traffic is automated. Knowing who\u0026#39;s human, who\u0026#39;s an agent, and who\u0026#39;s a malicious actor is core to Cloudflare\u0026#39;s strategy, and one of the primary values we sell to our customers.Cloudflare sits in front of more than 20% of the web. That vantage point lets us detect automated threats, fraud, and traffic manipulation at a scale and depth no one else can match. Turning that raw signal into something a human can understand, trust, and act on is one of the most interesting design problems in security today — and it\u0026#39;s the problem you\u0026#39;ll own.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Our products make probabilistic decisions in an adversarial environment. “Is this traffic truthfully representing who they are?” and \u0026quot;Can we trust this traffic?\u0026quot; doesn\u0026#39;t have a clean yes-or-no answer. Our objective is to minimize risk without ever having ground truth. Your job is to make that kind of reasoning legible and controllable to the people who rely on it, from the security analyst running an investigation to the marketing team trying to understand the performance of their most recent campaign.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;This role spans the full arc of how customers work with our product suite, from navigation, configuration, exploring and investigating their traffic, to proving the value of what Cloudflare\u0026#39;s network sees. We manage the end-to-end flow of server and network hardware into fully integrated data center racks to support our growing global network. global partners with the material readiness, capacity planning, and operational visibility needed to execute Cloudflare’s global expansion.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;What You’ll While this design maximizes hardware utilization, it creates a difficult distributed attribution problem. Machine-level telemetry tells us how loaded a server is, but not which product, customer, or upstream service is responsible for that load.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;MAPS (Metrics and Analytics for Product Segmentation) is a newly formed team building the core instrumentation, collection, and data platform to solve this from the ground up. We are architecting a system to continuously measure CPU, network bandwidth, memory, and storage utilization across the entire global fleet without sampling—attributing resource consumption both to the underlying system service and to the specific product, account, and zone being served.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;The data MAPS produces serves two critical functions at Cloudflare:\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ol\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Real-Time Control Plane: MAPS is the primary telemetry input for Cloudflare’s next-generation global load balancer, shifting traffic management from open-loop heuristics to closed-loop routing driven by real-time, per-service resource capacity and consumption (within seconds).\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Fleet Economics \u0026amp;amp; Capacity Planning: MAPS provides the long-term analytical dataset in ClickHouse used to map product demand forecasts to physical hardware requirements, calculate true cost-to-serve per product, and drive multi-year infrastructure investments.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ol\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;What You’ll Do\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You will work across the full lifecycle of a greenfield, high-throughput telemetry system running on every machine at the Cloudflare edge:\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Host-Level Instrumentation (\u0026quot;Outside View\u0026quot;): Build and maintain low-overhead Linux daemons (netacctd, maps_collector) in Rust and C that use eBPF (cgroup_skb) and cgroup v2 accounting to measure per-service resource consumption directly from the kernel.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;High-Performance Client Libraries (\u0026quot;Inside View\u0026quot;): Architect non-blocking, zero-allocation reporting SDKs in Rust and Go used by Cloudflare’s highest-throughput data-plane services to report per-request resource usage and product attribution over local Unix domain sockets.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Edge Aggregation \u0026amp;amp; Streaming: Build the per-machine collector daemon that ingests millions of events per second, performs bounded in-memory time-window aggregation, serves low-latency gRPC streams to the global load balancer, and flushes batch rollups to ClickHouse.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Reconciliation \u0026amp;amp; Correctness: Solve complex attribution problems—such as reconciling kernel-level cgroup measurements against application-reported metrics, and attributing resource usage when one multi-tenant service executes work on behalf of another.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Cross-Team Architecture: Partner directly with the engineering teams behind Cloudflare’s core proxies, runtimes, and storage engines to instrument their critical paths without degrading tail latency.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;What We’re Looking For\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Strong systems programming experience in Rust, Go, or C, with a solid grasp of memory layout, concurrency, and performance-critical code paths.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience designing and operating latency- and resource-sensitive server infrastructure or high-throughput data pipelines at scale.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Strong fundamentals in Linux systems internals—processes, cgroups, sockets, and how the kernel accounts for compute, memory, and I/O.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Proven ability to work across organizational boundaries: reading unfamiliar codebases, aligning with other infrastructure teams, and driving complex integrations to completion.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A pragmatic approach to owning outcomes—from kernel-level data collection and wire protocols (protobuf/Cap\u0026#39;n Proto) all the way to the analytical tables consumers query.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Bonus Points\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Hands-on experience writing and verifying eBPF programs, or deep familiarity with the Linux networking stack and scheduler.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience designing schemas and query patterns for distributed columnar databases (particularly ClickHouse) at high ingestion rates.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Background in profiling, benchmarking, and debugging Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a \u0026quot;normalized\u0026quot; problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/div\u0026gt;\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC,\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;About the team\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare\u0026#39;s network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers\u0026#39; traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare\u0026#39;s network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum).\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;About the role\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We\u0026#39;re looking for engineers who want to build the software that forwards, filters, and load-balances packets for a meaningful fraction of the internet. If you\u0026#39;ve worked on routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, or SDN data planes, and you\u0026#39;d like to do that in software, at Cloudflare\u0026#39;s scale, this is the role.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We\u0026#39;re moving towards a unified data plane platform that all of our L3/L4 products share. Instead of each product having its own data path, with its own configuration, performance work, and failure modes, we build a feature once and every product gets it.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Some of the things you\u0026#39;d work on:\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;The shared platform: packet I/O, a graph of processing stages, per-core steering, per-customer isolation, and upgrades that don\u0026#39;t drop traffic\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A userspace forwarding plane that gives each customer their own routing and forwarding, with traffic arriving and leaving over tunnels (GRE, IPsec) and direct connections\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A stateful packet firewall written in Rust: rule evaluation, rate limiting, intrusion detection, packet capture, and dual-stack IPv4/IPv6\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;An XDP-based L4 load balancer that touches nearly every connection into Cloudflare and forwards packets between servers and between data centers\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A fast path that uses XDP and eBPF to forward very large single flows at multiple Gbps\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Host networking: classifying each packet once and using that result everywhere on the server, instead of separate configs that can disagree\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Chasing down packet drops, latency, and throughput problems across a fleet of servers in hundreds of cities\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We write mostly Go and Rust (plus C for eBPF) on Linux, and the work ranges from XDP and the kernel network stack to userspace packet pipelines and the control planes that configure them.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You\u0026#39;ll build, deploy, and operate these systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You\u0026#39;ll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our team and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We\u0026#39;re looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done!\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Examples of desirable skills, knowledge, and experience\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Systems programming experience in Rust, Go, C, or C++\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A solid understanding of L3 and L4 networking: IP, TCP, UDP, routing and forwarding, tunneling (GRE, IPsec), NAT, connection tracking, and anycast\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience building data plane software: routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, VPN gateways, or SDN/NFV systems\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Linux networking: eBPF/XDP, tc, netfilter/nftables, network namespaces, sockets, etc.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;High-performance packet processing in user space or the kernel (e.g., AF_XDP, DPDK, VPP)\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Debugging, profiling, and optimizing systems where throughput and latency matter\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Building and operating large-scale, reliable, distributed systems\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Operating what you build: on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Reading unfamiliar code and safely evolving systems that have been in production for years\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Owning work end to end, from design through deployment, and working across teams to land shared solutions\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Clear written and verbal communication; Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a \u0026quot;normalized\u0026quot; problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/div\u0026gt;\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC,\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;About the team\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare\u0026#39;s network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers\u0026#39; traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare\u0026#39;s network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum).\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;About the role\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;For us, performance is a product feature. Customers notice single-flow throughput, packet loss, and latency right away, and every CPU cycle we spend on a packet is multiplied across every server in our network. We\u0026#39;re looking for engineers who love finding out where the time goes, and then making it go away.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Some of the things you\u0026#39;d work on:\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Pushing single large flows (e.g., one tunnel carrying a customer\u0026#39;s whole data center) to multiple Gbps and beyond, and making that performance consistent\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Finding out exactly where packets get dropped and why: NIC queues, interrupts and softirq, XDP, veth and namespaces, userspace rings, and everything in between\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;CPU placement: NUMA, RSS, core isolation, and steering traffic to the right cores on servers that also run many other services\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Cutting the CPU cost per packet in hot paths written in Rust, C, and Go: batching, cache-friendly data structures, fewer copies, fewer locks\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Measuring all of it: profiling with perf, eBPF tracing, and flame graphs; continuous profiling across the fleet; benchmarks in the lab and careful experiments in production\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Building the benchmark and test tooling that keeps performance regressions from shipping\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Helping shape a unified data plane platform so that it\u0026#39;s fast from the start\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We write mostly Go and Rust (plus C for eBPF) on Linux, and the work ranges from NIC configuration and the kernel network stack to userspace packet pipelines.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You\u0026#39;ll build, deploy, and operate these systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You\u0026#39;ll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our team and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We\u0026#39;re looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done!\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Examples of desirable skills, knowledge, and experience\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Systems programming experience in Rust, Go, C, or C++\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Performance analysis on Linux: perf, eBPF-based tracing (e.g., bpftrace, BCC), flame graphs, hardware counters\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A working model of modern CPUs and memory: caches, NUMA, branch prediction, SIMD, and how they show up in a profile\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Knowledge of how packets move through Linux: NIC queues, RSS, NAPI, GRO/GSO, softirq, and the socket layer\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience making high-throughput or low-latency systems faster, and proving it with good measurements\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A solid understanding of L3 and L4 networking: IP, TCP, UDP, and tunneling\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Building and operating large-scale, reliable, distributed systems\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Operating what you build: on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Reading unfamiliar code and safely evolving systems that have been in production for years\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Owning work end to end, from design through deployment, and working across teams to land shared solutions\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Clear written and verbal communication; we design in written specs and review each other\u0026#39;s work\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;Bonus points\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Tuning AF_XDP, DPDK, or other kernel-bypass systems\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Low-latency backgrounds such as trading systems, HPC, games, or storage\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Go runtime or Rust async performance work\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;NIC offloads and features (e.g., checksum, TSO/LRO, flow steering, SR-IOV)\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Contributions to the Linux kernel or open-source performance tooling\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3 data-path-to-node=\u0026quot;1\u0026quot;\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong data-path-to-node=\u0026quot;1\u0026quot;
